paragraphs.text: The Mightstone and Weakstone were the two halves of a Thran powerstone that played a major part in both the founding of Phyrexia and instigating the Brothers' War on Dominaria .

The planeswalker Dyfed cracked a large powerstone in half to establish a permanent portal between Dominaria and Phyrexia , creating what would become the Mightstone and Weakstone. Afterward, Yawgmoth secretly placed the two halves (the Mightstone and the Weakstone) inside Glacian to worsen his case of phthisis . While inside him, the two halves absorbed Glacian's essence, empowering them with his mastery of artifice, with the Mightstone being able to empower artifacts and the Weakstone to deactivate them. After Glacian's death, his wife Rebbec discovered Yawgmoth's evil nature and recombined the two halves to close the portal Dyfed had created, sealing him in Phyrexia. However, the cleave between the two remained, with Phyrexia awaiting the next time the stones separated.

Following the destruction of Halcyon in the Thran Civil War , the two stones remained in the Caves of Koilos for approximately 5000 years, until the ruins of the Thran capital were excavated by Tocasia and her two apprentices, the brothers Urza and Mishra . As they excavated the Hall of Tagsin , the two brothers uncovered the pedestal where the two stones were kept together. Urza took the Mightstone and Mishra the Weakstone, unwittingly reactivating the gate to Phyrexia. They also accidentally awoke the su-chi that guarded the vault, who then promptly attacked the brothers and their master. Urza tried to use his stone to stop them, but found that he had only made them stronger, the creatures only being stopped when Mishra used his stone against them.

As the excavation work wore on, the brothers became increasingly jealous of each other, each wanting to possess the other's stone. This came to a head back in the encampment, where they argued and became violent, using their respective stones against each other before accidentally killing Tocasia when she tried to calm them. After their master's death, the two brothers separated and, over the years, began building armies and claiming territories.

Urza's accumulation of political power was, in a sense, nearly inadvertent. He coveted knowledge of artifice, with Yotia's royal family guarding the Jalum Tome ; thus, the simplest solution was to marry into the lineage through crown princess Kayla bin-Kroog . The ceremonial miter of the Lord Protector was lined by many small powerstones, so Urza concluded becoming the coalition's military leader the most practical way to obtain them. However, his cold pragmatism did not make for a happy marriage.

Mishra fled to the desert, taking the Weakstone with him. He fell into the hands of the Fallaji , who enslaved him and took the stone from him. Mishra was later freed from labor works by Hajar , who knew him from Tocasia's camp, but the stone was not returned to him until later when Mishra accidentally summoned a dragon engine which attacked the Fallaji and killed the elder Qadir . Mishra and Hajar used the confusion to retrieve the stone so it could be used to stop the beast, but instead, Mishra found that he could control it . Using his new weapon, Mishra aided the Fallaji in expanding their power across Terisiare , beginning the Brothers' War . At one point, Gix attempted to steal the stone and murder Mishra in his sleep, but the stone protected both itself and its master, burning Gix's hand and pushing him away. Gix then decided to corrupt Mishra instead.

By some strange force of destiny, the estranged brothers ended up on opposing sides of what would have been a typical territorial dispute. Both were part of the retinues that attended Peace Summit at Korlinda , but their reunion was awkward but not hostile. The same could not be said about their superiors, though, with the impulsive slaying of Yotia's leader by the Fallaji Qadir being the first domino towards apocalypse.

Mishra's envy of the Mightstone escalated the dispute into armed conflict. The second summit at Kroog began without incident, despite the assassination, but the treaty as drafted by Mishra included the surrender of the Mightstone, something Kayla considered acceptable but Urza would not consider. The tipping point happened when Kayla was approached outside the negotiation table with a scheme: deliver the Mightstone personally to Mishra. Urza discovered them in flagrante, leading to the immediate collapse of negotiations and a declaration of war. The final straw was when the Qadir came across Kayla and Mishra's apprentice Ashnod escaping from Mishra's successful rout of Kroog: despite being aligned with Mishra and the Fallaji, the Qadir ordered Ashnod dead along the others, resulting in Ashnod killing the Qadir. Mishra would then ascend as Qadir and leader of the Fallaji. With both brothers each at the helm of their respective empires, their uncompromising conflict would engulf Dominaria.

At the climax of the long war, Urza used the Golgothian Sylex to obliterate his brother and his army. The blast also destroyed Urza's forces and leveled Argoth , but Urza himself survived thanks to his spark triggering. As he became a planeswalker , the Mightstone and the Weakstone merged with him, becoming his eyes. Despite his power and the power of planeswalkers in general, they were a weak point, as extracting them would kill him.

The two crystals remained embedded in Urza's head throughout his life as a planeswalker, still aiding in his creation of artifacts. The only occasion before Urza's death in which they were removed was when Urza returned to Serra's Realm to use the collapsing plane to power Weatherlight ' s planeshifting engine. He discovered that Serra had been forced to flee her realm after the Phyrexians attacked it and brought black mana corruption in their wake. Serra's replacement was the angel Radiant , who held Urza responsible for the devastation afflicting her plane. She trapped Urza inside Serra's Sanctum and attacked him, plucking the two stones from his eyes. Radiant then foolishly put the two stones together, triggering an explosion that killed the angel and restored Urza.

The stones were removed one last time following Yawgmoth's return to Dominaria . The only way to stop him was to complete the Legacy , so Gerrard Capashen had to remove the stones from Urza's eyes and combine them inside Karn 's chest. He did this, triggering a burst of energy that drove Yawgmoth from Dominaria while killing Gerrard and causing Karn to become a planeswalker. The combined stones merged with Karn, granting him the knowledge of both Glacian and Urza.

In Shattered Chains , the wizard Haakon is said to use "the Mightstone of Urza", which is described to match its original card art: "a clenched fist that glowed red". As the novel takes place from 4073 to 4074 AR when the Mightstone was still in the living Urza's eye, implying this must have been a forgery or replica of the true Mightstone. It was recovered by Gull and Greensleeves 's army after Haakon's capture.
